raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Add Ascend deployment choices to the MiniMax-M2.5 cookbook: a tested A2 eight-device configuration and a separately labelled A3 reference. Related task: https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/issues/1215

HiDevLab supplied A2 multi-card resources; A3 multi-card resources are unavailable for this contribution. The contributor is proceeding with A2 measurements plus the A3 reference. Hardware/performance equivalence and an A3 benchmark pass are not implied; acceptance of the adjusted scope remains subject to maintainer review.

## Changes

- Add an A2 selector for 8 x Ascend 910B4 / 32 GiB, TP8, ModelSlim W8A8 main weights, BF16, one request at a time, and no EAGLE3 draft model. Model/tokenizer paths are editable and shell-quoted.
- Use the verified selector settings `--mem-fraction-static 0.96 --max-total-tokens 4096`, context 4096, chunked prefill 128, and graph/radix cache disabled.
- Keep the A3 8-card / 16-die W8A8 + EAGLE3 recipe separately labelled as an unvalidated reference.
- Add measured A2 performance results and reproduction commands in section 5.5, using a separate configuration supporting concurrency up to 8.
- Preserve earlier capacity failures and corrected results.
- Add 13 command-generator regression tests covering the A2 preset, existing platforms, and platform transitions.

## A2 hardware results

The selector configuration allocated 4096 KV tokens on every rank. Six simple answer checks passed with natural stops, and six serial native probes with exact inputs of 64, 128, 256, 1024, 2048, and 3500 tokens each produced the requested 128 output tokens. Post-test health was HTTP 200. These are functional checks, not GPQA accuracy.

The separate performance configuration used static memory fraction 0.97, a measured 16384-token KV pool, context 8192, and up to eight requests. The installed official SGLang benchmark completed all 10 planned runs: **76/76 measured requests succeeded**, with exact input-token lengths and 128 output tokens each. Every post-run health check returned HTTP 200.

| Input/output tokens | Concurrency | Runs x requests | Mean output throughput (tokens/s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 128/128 | 1 | 1 x 4 | 4.266 |
| 128/128 | 4 | 3 x 8 | 16.731 |
| 128/128 | 8 | 3 x 8 | 32.457 |
| 1024/128 | 8 | 3 x 8 | 13.694 |

Repeated groups use seeds 17, 29, and 43. The guide includes mean/min/max throughput and latency, workload generation, commands, and interpretation limits. Inputs are locally authored synthetic text in ShareGPT-compatible format, not the ShareGPT dataset. These short measurements differ from the A3 3500/1500-token reference and do not establish its 50 ms TPOT target or sustained stability.

Runtime: SGLang 0.5.14.dev172+gf308abc05, Torch 2.10.0+cpu, TorchNPU 2.10.0, Transformers 5.8.1, kernel 2026.5.1, CANN 9.0.0, driver 25.5.2. The supplied source tree had packaging-file modifications. An image digest and immutable model revision were not captured.

## Accuracy status and remaining work

The full GPQA Diamond evaluation is incomplete. Its bounded A2 protocol retains all 198 original questions, the pinned SGLang simple-evals prompt/answer parser, temperature 1, and a 6144-token output cap. All 198 tokenization prechecks passed at context 9216; the earlier 8192-context precheck rejected one oversized prompt before generating any answers. No question was cropped or omitted.

A first-four pilot completed with four correct answers, natural stops, and no capped outputs or protocol errors. Completion lengths were 2033, 5689, 1392, and 1205 tokens in original question order. These records are preserved; they are not a full-dataset accuracy result. No normal-accuracy conclusion is claimed.

On September 24, the additional 200 HiDevLab card-hours became available. The concurrency-8 continuation passed service identity/input-length checks but stopped admitting requests after KV pressure and retraction led to 1800-second HTTP timeouts. It retained 18 terminal records: 12 correct, 5 transport timeouts, and no output-cap terminations. This is an incomplete run, not a full-dataset score. All answers, timeout streams, logs, and cleanup evidence were preserved and backed up.

An independent concurrency-2 GPQA run was then launched with the same prompt, parser, temperature, seeds, output cap and request deadline. It was deliberately stopped on September 24 after repeated output-cap terminations and a review of the compute cost. New admissions stopped through the controlled pause mechanism, and both in-flight requests were retained before cleanup. The final incomplete run contains **26 terminal records: 16 correct, 9 output-cap terminations and no transport/protocol errors**. No C8 answer was imported or selected against a C2 answer. The full-198 accuracy remains unavailable; these are diagnostic records, not a full-dataset score or a normal-accuracy claim. All raw records, streams, logs and cleanup evidence were backed up with verified hashes.

The issue requires accuracy validation but does not prescribe GPQA or 198 questions. The bounded GPQA protocol differs from the A3 EvalScope reference and remains incomplete. A separate predeclared GSM8K deployment-regression protocol now uses five training examples, three independent pilot test items, and 50 frozen disjoint test items. The three pilot items all ended naturally and scored correctly, with 1060, 496 and 1603 output tokens; this establishes feasibility only. The frozen 50-item run completed on September 24: **49/50 correct (98% on this fixed subset), 50 natural stops, zero output-cap terminations and zero request errors**, in 9444.6 seconds of client runtime. All 50 unique terminal records and tokenizer prechecks were verified; independent final-content rescoring agreed with the summary. The complete archive and all 172 manifest hashes were verified locally, all eight NPUs had no remaining processes, and the instance was shut down. It uses client concurrency 1, temperature 1, a 6144-token output cap and context 9216, with no retries or replacement items, and a six-hour total instance window. The three pilot answers are excluded from the 50-item score. Even a completed subset is not full GSM8K or GPQA accuracy.

The independent reference-length A2 benchmark completed all 6 measured requests: 3 seeds (1, 17, 29), 2 requests each at client concurrency 2, exact 3500 input / 1500 output tokens. Three 32-token warmup requests are excluded. Inputs are locally authored synthetic text in ShareGPT-compatible format. The eager TP8/ModelSlim/BF16 service used context 9216, KV 16384, memory fraction 0.97, chunked prefill 128, and max-running-requests 8. Across the three run-level measurements, mean output throughput was 8.004 tokens/s (range 7.896–8.065), mean TPOT 243.163 ms (range 241.222–246.570), mean TTFT 10.317 s, and mean end-to-end latency 374.818 s. These means/ranges describe run-level aggregates, not individual-request extrema. The full archive and all 46 evidence hashes were independently verified; owned processes were cleared and the performance instance window was shut down. An earlier missing-file preflight failure occurred before model startup or benchmark requests and is retained in the archive. These A2 low-concurrency measurements do not establish the A3 C320 / 50 ms target. Cookbook sections 5.6 and 5.7 now include these measured results, reproduction commands and the frozen regression protocol. This PR is ready for review. Maintainer review is requested for the documented A2 measurements plus A3 reference and the explicitly bounded validation scope.

A bounded eager-versus-decode-graph diagnostic was completed on September 24 with unchanged TP8/ModelSlim/BF16, context 9216, KV 16384 and static memory fraction 0.97. The eager group completed all 9 measured synthetic 128-input/128-output requests (3 at C1, 6 at C2), plus 3 excluded warmup requests. Mean client-observed TPOT estimates were 236.98 ms at C1 and 241.54 ms at C2. NPU graph capture for batches 1/2 completed, but subsequent startup warmup / graph-input update raised torch.OutOfMemoryError (507033 / Memory_Allocation_Failure); health remained unavailable and no graph measurement requests ran. The operator stopped the supervisor through its cleanup handler after the observed failure; no memory retuning or retry was performed. The complete archive and 93 evidence-file hashes were verified, owned processes were cleared, and the instance was shut down. This diagnoses only the frozen configuration: it establishes neither graph speedup nor general A2 graph incompatibility, accuracy, or A3 parity.

## Validation

The 13 command-generator tests and shared cookbook configuration check passed. Applicable pre-commit checks, git diff --check, and Mintlify build validation passed for the new performance documentation. Local preview verified the revised tables without overlapping text. Independent review checked numerical claims against archived raw benchmark outputs.

For the new evidence documentation, all 13 command-generator tests, cookbook configuration checks, applicable pre-commit hooks, git diff --check and a fresh Mintlify build validation passed. The published MDX blob was fetched and matched the locally verified file byte for byte. GitHub Lint passed for head 27e1120 (run 36006583043), including pre-commit, cookbook authoring contracts and Mintlify broken-links. The previous Extra and Extra AMD runs stopped at the Draft PR gate, before runtime tests. The PR is now ready for review and includes main at 4142235c2 through merge commit 6283398. On this new head, Extra and Extra AMD pass the Draft gate but stop at the missing run-ci label; the Extra workflow also requires run-ci-extra. Maintainers can decide whether these additional suites are needed and apply the required CI labels. Base CI passed; Lint is still running. Skipped runtime jobs are not runtime passes.

Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #39596061698](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39596061698)<!-- slot:pr-test:end -->
Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #39596061370](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39596061370)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end -->
Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd:start -->:heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.<!-- slot:pr-test-amd:end -->
<!-- pr-states:end -->

The PR title fails the pr-title.yml CI check. Please rename it to:
`[Doc] [NPU] cookbook: add tested A2 deployment and A3 reference for MiniMax-M2.5`

`docs/scripts/check_minimax_m25_deployment.mjs`
sits in the `docs/scripts/` root, but CI (.github/workflows/lint.yml) only runs
`docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs` and `node --test docs/scripts/tests/*.test.mjs`,
so this file is never executed. Please move it to
`docs/scripts/tests/minimax-m25-deployment.test.mjs`
The NPU's formula structure is quite different from other devices.

files.patch:
@@ -1,5 +1,6 @@
 ---
 title: MiniMax-M2.5
+description: "Deploy MiniMax-M2.5 with SGLang on NVIDIA, AMD, or Ascend A2, with an Ascend A3 reference configuration."
 metatags:
     description: "Deploy MiniMax-M2.5 with SGLang - community contribution guide for MiniMax M2.5 model deployment."
 ---
@@ -23,7 +24,7 @@ For more details, please refer to the [official MiniMax-M2.5 announcement](https
 
 SGLang offers multiple installation methods. You can choose the most suitable installation method based on your hardware platform and requirements.
 
-Please refer to the [official SGLang installation guide](../../../docs/get-started/install) for installation instructions.
+Please refer to the [official SGLang installation guide](/docs/get-started/install) for installation instructions.
 
 **For AMD MI300X/MI325X/MI355X GPUs:**
 
@@ -35,19 +36,75 @@ docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.9-rocm720-mi30x
 docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.9-rocm720-mi35x
 ```
 
+### Ascend A2 prerequisites (smoke tested)
+
+Select **Ascend A2** for the tested **8 × Ascend 910B4, 32 GiB HBM per device** configuration. It loads the W8A8 main model with TP=8 and serves one request at a time, without a draft model. The final run passed six simple chat checks and six synthetic generation probes, including 3500 input tokens plus 128 output tokens; see [the validation record](#5-4-ascend-a2-smoke-validation) for the runtime versions and test limits.
+
+1. Prepare a compatible Ascend NPU runtime using the [NPU installation guide](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/installation). The tested runtime was SGLang `0.5.14.dev172+gf308abc05`, TorchNPU 2.10.0, and sgl-kernel-npu 2026.5.1. Follow-up inspection recorded CANN 9.0.0 and driver 25.5.2. An image digest was not captured; the A3 image below was not validated for this A2 run.
+2. Run `npu-smi info` inside the container and confirm all eight 910B4 devices are visible and healthy. Reserve space for the approximately 230.82 GB main weights, download cache, and runtime.
+3. Download the complete main model repository, including tokenizer and configuration files:
+
+```bash Command
+python -m pip install modelscope
+modelscope download --model Eco-Tech/MiniMax-M2.5-w8a8-QuaRot \
+  --local_dir /models/MiniMax-M2.5-w8a8-QuaRot
+```
+
+Enter absolute paths inside your container in the selector. Both directories default to the complete model directory. If you keep tokenizer files separately, use files from the same model revision and set **Tokenizer Directory** accordingly. The original experiment used separate metadata and weights directories, as recorded in section 5.4.
+
+### Ascend A3 prerequisites (unvalidated reference)
+
+The A3 selector provides **one Ascend A3 node with 8 cards / 16 NPU dies**, running prefill and decode together (PD co-located). It uses W8A8 weights and EAGLE3 speculative decoding. Each A3 card contains two dies; a cloud allocation labelled "1 NPU" is not a full node. The [minimum recommended W8A8 configuration](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/minimax_m2_5#model-weights) is 4 cards / 8 dies with 64 GB per die, while this preset requires all 16 dies.
+
+<Note>
+This recipe is based on the upstream Ascend best practice. Hardware validation of the generated A3 cookbook command is pending; the reference accuracy and performance values below are not measurements of this recipe. The tested A2 selector is a separate low-concurrency configuration and does not validate the A3 preset.
+</Note>
+
+1. Set up the Ascend runtime using the [MiniMax-M2.5 installation instructions](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/tutorials/minimax_m2_5#installation). The reference environment uses CANN 9.0.0 and `quay.io/ascend/sglang:cann9.0.0-a3-v0.5.16`. Map `/dev/davinci0` through `/dev/davinci15` and mount your model directory into the container, for example `-v /path/to/models:/models`.
+2. Check device health and allocation with `npu-smi info` inside the container. Confirm that all 16 dies are visible. For source builds, follow [installation with NPU support](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/installation), keep the CANN, TorchNPU, and kernel versions compatible, and record the SGLang commit you install.
+3. Reserve space for the **230.82 GB** main weights, the draft model, download cache, and at least **30 GB** for the container image. Download both models below, or reuse complete copies from shared storage.
+
+| Role | Model | Directory inside the container |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| W8A8 main model | [Eco-Tech/MiniMax-M2.5-w8a8-QuaRot](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/MiniMax-M2.5-w8a8-QuaRot) | `/models/MiniMax-M2.5-w8a8-QuaRot` |
+| EAGLE3 draft model | [sgl-npu/MiniMax-M2.5-eagel-model-0318](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/sgl-npu/MiniMax-M2.5-eagel-model-0318) | `/models/MiniMax-M2.5-eagel-model-0318` |
+
+The draft repository identifier contains `eagel`; use that exact spelling. Keep its `custom_eagle3` Python package alongside the draft weights. The generated command adds this directory to `PYTHONPATH` and sets `SGLANG_EXTERNAL_MODEL_PACKAGE=custom_eagle3`.
+
+You can download the weights with the [ModelScope CLI](https://github.com/modelscope/modelscope/blob/master/docs/source/command.md#download):
+
+```bash Command
+python3 -m pip install modelscope
+modelscope download --model Eco-Tech/MiniMax-M2.5-w8a8-QuaRot \
+  --local_dir /models/MiniMax-M2.5-w8a8-QuaRot
+modelscope download --model sgl-npu/MiniMax-M2.5-eagel-model-0318 \
+  --local_dir /models/MiniMax-M2.5-eagel-model-0318
+```
+
+Before launching, run `ip -brief address` and select an interface available inside the container for both HCCL and Gloo. The selector defaults to `lo` for this single-node setup.
+
+For comparable performance, use the host settings from the [selected 8-card reference](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/model-deployment/best-practices/minimax_m2_5#minimax-m2-5-w8a8-8p-in3k5-out1k5-50ms). These affect the whole host; apply them on the dedicated benchmark server before running the generated command:
+
+```bash Command
+echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
+sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
+sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
+sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
+```
+
 ## 3. Model Deployment
 
 This section provides deployment configurations optimized for different hardware platforms and use cases.
 
 ### 3.1 Basic Configuration
 
-**Interactive Command Generator**: Use the configuration selector below to automatically generate the appropriate deployment command for your hardware platform, deployment strategy, and feature capabilities.
+**Interactive Command Generator**: Select your hardware to generate the deployment command. For **Ascend A2**, complete the A2 prerequisites, expand **Deployment paths**, and enter the model and tokenizer directories; the command reproduces the tested single-request settings on port 31216. For **Ascend A3**, complete its separate prerequisites, expand **Deployment paths and network**, enter both model directories as absolute paths inside the container, and set the HCCL / Gloo interface. The unvalidated A3 preset uses 3,500 input and 1,500 output tokens as its reference workload.
 
 <MiniMaxM25Deployment />
 
 ### 3.2 Configuration Tips
 
-**Key Parameters:**
+**GPU parameters:** The following recommendations apply to the NVIDIA and AMD recipes. The Ascend presets use the separate settings described below.
 
 <table style={{width: "100%", borderCollapse: "collapse", tableLayout: "fixed"}}>
   <colgroup>

+dataset = out / "synthetic-prompts.json"

+cases = ([(128, 1, 4, 17)]

+    with (out / f"{name}.log").open("w", encoding="utf-8") as log:

+    if len(rows) != 1:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Expected exactly one result in {result}")
+    row = rows[0]

+            and row["output_lens"] == [128] * count
+            and len(row["errors"]) == count and not any(row["errors"])):

+| Metric | Mean | Min–max |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Output throughput (tok/s) | 8.004 | 7.896–8.065 |
+| Total throughput (tok/s) | 26.680 | 26.319–26.882 |
+| Mean TTFT (ms) | 10317.118 | 10267.749–10365.114 |
+| Mean TPOT (ms) | 243.163 | 241.222–246.570 |
+| Mean E2E (s) | 374.818 | 371.957–379.927 |
+
+These are arithmetic means and minimum–maximum values across the three run-level means or rates, not request extrema. Per-run percentiles are retained separately and are not averaged. Six measured requests provide a bounded performance observation, not a sustained-load or stability result.
+
+To reproduce, generate `minimax-a2-perf/synthetic-prompts.json` using the data-creation portion of section 5.5.2, launch the server with context 9216, and run the following from that working directory. Use the same model/tokenizer paths as the server, and retain each JSONL and log, including failures:
+
+```bash Command
+set -euo pipefail
+mkdir -p minimax-a2-reference-perf
+for SEED in 1 17 29; do
+  RESULT="minimax-a2-reference-perf/in3500-out1500-c2-n2-seed${SEED}.jsonl"
+  test ! -e "$RESULT"
+  python -m sglang.bench_serving \
+    --backend sglang --base-url http://127.0.0.1:31216 \
+    --model /workspace/issue1215/model \
+    --tokenizer /workspace/issue1215/metadata \
+    --dataset-name random --dataset-path minimax-a2-perf/synthetic-prompts.json \
+    --random-input-len 3500 --random-output-len 1500 --random-range-ratio 1 \
+    --tokenize-prompt --num-prompts 2 --max-concurrency 2 \
+    --request-rate inf --temperature 0 --seed "$SEED" \
+    --warmup-requests 1 --flush-cache --output-details --disable-tqdm \
+    --output-file "$RESULT" 2>&1 | tee "${RESULT%.jsonl}.log"
+done
+```
+
+Check every result for `completed=2`, input lengths `[3500,3500]`, output lengths `[1500,1500]`, and two empty error entries before aggregating it. Verify server health after each run. A successful process exit alone is insufficient to establish those conditions.
+
+### 5.7 Ascend A2 fixed 50-question GSM8K regression
+
+On September 24, 2026, a **preselected 50-question deployment regression completed with 49/50 correct (98%)**, zero capped outputs, zero transport/protocol errors, and no missing or duplicate questions. This is a bounded GSM8K test subset, not full GSM8K accuracy, an EvalScope result, GPQA accuracy, or evidence of A3 parity.
+
+The run used the same A2 hardware, W8A8 weights, and runtime as above. The server used context 9216, maximum running requests **2**, memory fraction 0.97, and KV limit 16384; all other launch settings matched section 5.6. The client submitted **one request at a time** to `/v1/chat/completions`, with `temperature=1.0`, `max_tokens=6144`, and generation seed `42 + original test row index`. The reasoning parser remained `minimax`; scoring used only final answer content.
+
+The protocol was frozen before an independent three-question pilot:
+
+1. Use the MIT-licensed [official GSM8K data at revision 3101c7d5072418e28b9008a6636bde82a006892c](https://github.com/openai/grade-school-math/tree/3101c7d5072418e28b9008a6636bde82a006892c/grade_school_math/data). Take training rows 0–4 as five worked demonstrations.
+2. Shuffle all 1319 test-row indices with Python `random.Random(20260924).shuffle`. Reserve the first three indices for the independent pilot and use the next 50, in order, for this regression. Do not include pilot answers in the result or select, replace, reorder, or drop questions based on observed answers.
+3. Build a single user message by joining the five `Question: ...\nAnswer: ...` demonstrations with two newlines, then append the test question as `Question: ...\nAnswer:`. Preserve the training answers, including their worked solutions. Apply the deployed MiniMax chat template through the chat endpoint.
+4. Before any generation, tokenize all 50 messages with the server and verify that each prompt plus the 6144-token output allowance fits context 9216. Submit each frozen question exactly once, with a per-request wall limit of 1800 seconds. Stop new submissions on a transport/protocol error; do not retry or resume a failed run.
+5. Parse only final content using the pinned runtime's last-number rule: remove commas, find matches of `-?\d+\.?\d*`, and parse the last match numerically. Compare it with the gold answer parsed the same way. A missing number, wrong answer, length cap, or transport/protocol error scores zero. Keep the denominator fixed at 50; report an incomplete run as incomplete rather than a full score.
+
+The selection can be reconstructed without model access:
+
+```python Example
+import random
+
+indices = list(range(1319))
+random.Random(20260924).shuffle(indices)
+pilot_ids = indices[:3]       # Excluded from regression scoring.
+regression_ids = indices[3:53]
+assert len(set(regression_ids)) == 50
+assert not set(pilot_ids).intersection(regression_ids)
+```
+
+| Check | Observed result |
+| --- | --- |
+| Unique completed questions | 50/50 |
+| Correct final answers | 49/50 (98%) |
+| Wrong final answers | 1 |
+| Length-capped responses | 0 |
+| Transport/protocol errors | 0 |
+| Completion-token range | 292–2507 |
+
+All 50 prompts passed preflight. The client elapsed time, including preflight, was 9444.598 seconds; it is not a per-request latency benchmark. The downloaded run's 172 manifest entries passed hash verification, and rescoring the preserved final answers with the declared parser reproduced 49/50. Preserve the frozen IDs, prompt hashes, parameters, every response, and raw SSE when reproducing the regression. This result tests the declared subset and parsing protocol; it does not establish full-dataset accuracy, long-context quality, sustained stability, or the unvalidated A3 recipe's acceptance criteria.
